report_name: GPU Trace Frontend Necessity Go/No-Go Verdict
provenance: BERT encoder layer training slice, measured via instrumented simulator run on 2026-05-04
verdict: INCONCLUSIVE: simulator frontend_share=57.6% justifies investigation, but complete-flow P_trace_to_sim=11.5% (<15%) when trace export dominates. Frontend restructuring is worth investigating for simulator iteration speed, but end-to-end burden is dominated by trace generation.

basis.satisfied_by: P_trace_to_sim_slice = 11.5% does NOT exceed 15% in complete flow metric. However, simulator-only frontend_share = 57.6% — the frontend dominates inside the simulator.
basis.note: The plan defines T_kernel_to_sim_done including T_kernel_or_trace_export. With 180s trace export, the denominator grows from 46.9s to 225.2s, reducing P_trace_to_sim from 55.2% to 11.5%.

caveats: Simulator run was bounded at 50000 cycles (9 of 77 kernels simulated)
BERT pretraining full step and Llama workloads remain modeled/placeholder
This is an early-stage engineering gate, not a final paper claim threshold
status: Gate D PASS — go/no-go verdict based on measured claim-bearing data
